# azure-access-management has no third-party dependencies.
#
# This file and [project] in pyproject.toml say the same thing: `dependencies`
# there is empty, and the one optional extra is `live`. Installing is
# `pip install <this folder>`; `pip install "<this folder>[live]"` adds
# azure-identity for hosts that want a ready-made credential object, and no
# module here imports it.
#
# Standard library only, on purpose: this skill is dropped into repositories
# that already have an opinion about their dependency tree, and an access tool
# that drags in an SDK is one that does not get adopted.
#
# Live transports, both optional and both lazily constructed:
#   * AzureCliTransport  — shells out to `az rest`; needs the Azure CLI on PATH,
#     which is not a Python dependency. READ-ONLY: `az rest` reports no HTTP
#     status, so it cannot tell 201 from 202 from the 409 that means "already
#     exists", and it refuses mutating methods rather than guessing.
#   * TokenCredentialTransport — takes any object with `get_token(audience)`, so
#     `azure-identity` is the caller's dependency if they want it, never this
#     package's. Required for `apply` and `revoke`, because those need the real
#     status off the wire.
#
# Nothing below this line. If that changes, it changes here first.
